html:
The escalating conflict between the US and Iran and its far-reaching global economic consequences emerged as the dominant theme, with US president Trump delivering a stark address at the UN General Assembly while new US economic pressures threaten to cut off Iranian air travel. Meanwhile, Iran signaled its readiness to reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz under certain conditions, even as it claimed new military advances and warned of escalating its response to any further attacks.

US-Iran Tensions: US president Trump addressed the UN General Assembly, threatening to "annihilate" Iran if a deal is not reached, while also asserting that Iran will make a deal after the US midterm elections. The G7 condemned "in the strongest terms" Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and urged Iran to stop arming the Houthis, warning that escalating fighting in Yemen jeopardizes global energy security. Simultaneously, the Iranian Army announced it destroyed an 'Orbiter' reconnaissance drone over the Strait of Hormuz, and the IRGC claimed it successfully tested a weapon designed to target US aircraft carriers.

Economic Fallout: The global economic impact of the Iran war continued to deepen, with British homeowners paying more on mortgages as borrowing costs rise, and JP Morgan admitting it cannot forecast an end to the conflict due to US president Trump. Further exacerbating economic pressures, the US Treasury chief announced that Iranian airlines are slated to be "shut down" on September 23, a move that has already led Turkish Airlines to suspend all Iran flights until March 2027 and Iraq to halt Iranian carriers. Shipping traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz has dropped, with vessels now only trickling through.

Geopolitical Flashpoints: In Eastern Europe, Russia and Ukraine traded deadly strikes, including a Russian drone attack that killed three children and a woman in the Kyiv region, as Ukraine's Zelenskyy prepares to meet US president Trump. Lithuania's PM told BBC Newsnight that the nation feels "constantly threatened" by Moscow but is ready to "fight back" if attacked. Concurrently, US president Trump stated the US plans to build "two very major" bases in Greenland as a new deal on Arctic security between the US, Greenland, and Denmark is being signed, prompting mixed reactions among Greenlanders.

UN Agenda & Global Challenges: UN Secretary-General Guterres used his final address to the General Assembly to warn that "the fault lines in our world are widening" and "cracks have become canyons," urging leaders to regulate artificial intelligence, end wars, focus on climate change, and overhaul UN institutions. Global leaders, having set ambitious goals in 2015 to reduce inequality, end hunger, and boost education by 2030, have made little progress more than a decade later. Nepal's Environment Minister demanded "climate justice" and compensation from the UN-backed Loss and Damage Fund after devastating floods, while the UN climate change body faces accusations of conflict of interest and Saudi influence.

US-China AI Race: The US-China AI competition also gained prominence, with US president Trump indicating a move toward regulating artificial intelligence by forming a new task force and appointing a special envoy. As a summit between US president Trump and China's Xi Jinping nears, Europe is reportedly caught in the middle of this rivalry between erratic US trade policy and Beijing's export machine.

Regional Security Concerns: In the Middle East, Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant warned that if an Israeli soldier or civilian is abducted, the entire city of Gaza will be evacuated. This statement follows reports of two Palestinians, including a child, killed by Israeli gunfire in Gaza, and hundreds of Israeli settlers, including an Israeli minister, storming the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound under police protection, drawing condemnation from Jordan and the Arab League. The US has also banned Palestinian Authority officials from entering the country for the UN General Assembly for the second consecutive year.
